/-!
# Covering problem of Radó

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Covering problem of Rado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/covering_problem_of_Rado)
-/

open MeasureTheory

namespace CoveringProblemOfRado

/-- An axis-parallel square in the Euclidean plane, with positive side length. -/
structure AxisParallelSquare where
  lower : Fin 2 → ℝ
  side : ℝ
  side_pos : 0 < side

/-- The closed set of points covered by an axis-parallel square. -/
def AxisParallelSquare.carrier (Q : AxisParallelSquare) : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ) :=
  {x | ∀ j, Q.lower j ≤ x j ∧ x j ≤ Q.lower j + Q.side}

/-- The largest area covered by a subfamily whose square interiors are pairwise disjoint. -/
noncomputable def largestDisjointArea {n : ℕ} (S : Fin n → AxisParallelSquare) : ENNReal :=
  sSup {a | ∃ I : Finset (Fin n),
    (I : Set (Fin n)).PairwiseDisjoint (fun i ↦ interior (S i).carrier) ∧
      a = volume (⋃ i ∈ I, (S i).carrier)}

/--
**Covering problem of Radó.** Among all finite nonempty families of axis-parallel squares of
arbitrary positive side lengths whose union has Lebesgue area $1$, how small can the largest area
covered by a subfamily be when the interiors of its squares are pairwise disjoint? Equivalently,
determine the greatest lower bound below.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado :
    IsGLB {a | ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n) (S : Fin n → AxisParallelSquare),
      volume (⋃ i, (S i).carrier) = 1 ∧ a = largestDisjointArea S} answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end CoveringProblemOfRado

/-!
# Covering problem of Radó

The problem asks for the least guaranteed area of a pairwise interior-disjoint subfamily of a
finite family of axis-parallel squares whose union has area one. Radó conjectured that this
constant was $1/4$, but Ajtai disproved this candidate. The exact constant remains unknown.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Covering problem of Rado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/covering_problem_of_Rado)
- Miklós Ajtai, *The solution of a problem of T. Radó* (1973)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory

namespace CoveringProblemOfRado

/--
Radó's proposed answer $1/4$ to the covering problem is false: there is a nonempty finite family
of axis-parallel squares of positive side length whose union has area one, but every subfamily
with pairwise disjoint interiors has total area strictly less than $1/4$. Squares are represented
by their centers and open interiors, so touching along their boundaries is allowed.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (center : Fin n → ℝ²) (side : Fin n → ℝ),
      0 < n ∧ (∀ i, 0 < side i) ∧
      volume (⋃ i, {p : ℝ² |
        |p 0 - center i 0| < side i / 2 ∧ |p 1 - center i 1| < side i / 2}) = 1 ∧
      ∀ t : Finset (Fin n),
        (t : Set (Fin n)).PairwiseDisjoint (fun i ↦ {p : ℝ² |
          |p 0 - center i 0| < side i / 2 ∧ |p 1 - center i 1| < side i / 2}) →
        ∑ i ∈ t, side i ^ 2 < 1 / 4 := by
  sorry

end CoveringProblemOfRado

A finite family is indexed by `Fin n`, with `0 < n`; each square has an arbitrary center in `ℝ²` and an arbitrary positive real side length.

Squares are represented by their open interiors using strict coordinate inequalities. Thus `PairwiseDisjoint` means non-overlapping interiors and permits boundary contact, as specified in the decomposition.
The unit-area normalization uses Lebesgue volume of the union. For an interior-disjoint subfamily, its covered area is represented by the sum of the squares of its side lengths.

Although the list entry is marked open because the exact constant remains unknown, the fixed decomposition asks for Ajtai's established refutation of the 1/4 candidate; accordingly the stated proposition is tagged `research solved`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Covering problem of Rado

If the union of finitely many axis-parallel squares in the plane has unit area, how small can
the largest area covered by a pairwise disjoint subfamily of the squares be?

Tibor Radó (1928) proved that one can always find a disjoint subfamily covering area at least
$1/9$, and conjectured that the answer is $1/4$. Ajtai (1973) disproved this conjecture with a
family for which every disjoint subfamily covers area at most $1/4 - 1/1728$. The best bounds
currently known are $1/8.4797 \le F \le 1/4 - 1/384$ (Bereg, Dumitrescu and Jiang, 2010).
The exact value is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Covering problem of Rado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/covering_problem_of_Rado)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ra28] Radó, T., _Sur un problème relatif à un théorème de Vitali_.
  Fundamenta Mathematicae 11 (1928): 228–229.
- [Aj73] Ajtai, M., _The solution of a problem of T. Radó_.
  Bull. Acad. Polon. Sci. Sér. Sci. Math. Astronom. Phys. 21 (1973): 61–63.
- [BDJ10] Bereg, S., Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., _On covering problems of Rado_.
  Algorithmica 57 (2010): 538–561. doi:10.1007/s00453-009-9298-z
-/

open EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory

namespace CoveringProblemOfRado

/--
The open axis-parallel square $(a, a + r) \times (b, b + r)$ with lower left corner
`c = (a, b)` and side length `r`.

Squares are taken open, so that two squares are `Disjoint` exactly when their interiors do not
overlap: squares that only touch along their boundaries count as disjoint. This does not affect
any area, since boundaries have measure zero.
-/
def axisParallelSquare (c : ℝ²) (r : ℝ) : Set ℝ² :=
  {p | c 0 < p 0 ∧ p 0 < c 0 + r ∧ c 1 < p 1 ∧ p 1 < c 1 + r}

/-- A set `s` in the plane is an axis-parallel square (of positive side length). -/
def IsAxisParallelSquare (s : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ (c : ℝ²) (r : ℝ), 0 < r ∧ s = axisParallelSquare c r

/-- An axis-parallel square is the preimage of a product of open intervals. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem axisParallelSquare_eq_preimage (c : ℝ²) (r : ℝ) :
    axisParallelSquare c r =
      (@WithLp.ofLp 2 (Fin 2 → ℝ)) ⁻¹' (Set.pi Set.univ fun i => Set.Ioo (c i) (c i + r)) := by
  ext p
  simp [axisParallelSquare, Fin.forall_fin_two, and_assoc]

/-- The volume of an axis-parallel square of side length `r` is `r ^ 2`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem volume_axisParallelSquare (c : ℝ²) (r : ℝ) :
    volume (axisParallelSquare c r) = ENNReal.ofReal r ^ 2 := by
  rw [axisParallelSquare_eq_preimage,
    (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin 2)).measure_preimage
      (MeasurableSet.univ_pi fun _ => measurableSet_Ioo).nullMeasurableSet,
    Real.volume_pi_Ioo]
  simp [sq]

/-- The area of an axis-parallel square of side length `r ≥ 0` is `r ^ 2`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem volume_real_axisParallelSquare (c : ℝ²) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) :
    volume.real (axisParallelSquare c r) = r ^ 2 := by
  rw [measureReal_def, volume_axisParallelSquare, ← ENNReal.ofReal_pow hr,
    ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (by positivity)]

/--
The largest area covered by a pairwise disjoint subfamily of a finite family `S` of sets in
the plane.
-/
noncomputable def maxDisjointArea (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : ℝ :=
  sSup {volume.real (⋃₀ (I : Set (Set ℝ²))) |
    (I : Finset (Set ℝ²)) (_ : I ⊆ S) (_ : (I : Set (Set ℝ²)).PairwiseDisjoint id)}

/--
The set of values of `maxDisjointArea S`, where `S` ranges over the finite families of
axis-parallel squares whose union has unit area.
-/
def radoValues : Set ℝ :=
  {maxDisjointArea S | (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) (_ : ∀ s ∈ S, IsAxisParallelSquare s)
    (_ : volume.real (⋃₀ (S : Set (Set ℝ²))) = 1)}

/-- For a family consisting of a single set of finite volume, the largest area covered by a
disjoint subfamily is the area of that set. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem maxDisjointArea_singleton (s : Set ℝ²) (hs : volume s ≠ ⊤) :
    maxDisjointArea {s} = volume.real s := by
  apply IsGreatest.csSup_eq
  refine ⟨⟨{s}, subset_rfl, by simp, by simp⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro _ ⟨I, hI, -, rfl⟩
  exact measureReal_mono (by simpa using Set.sUnion_mono (Finset.coe_subset.mpr hI)) hs

/--
A single unit square is a family of axis-parallel squares with union of unit area, and its
largest disjoint subfamily covers area `1`. In particular, `radoValues` is nonempty, so it has
a greatest lower bound.
-/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem one_mem_radoValues : 1 ∈ radoValues := by
  refine ⟨{axisParallelSquare 0 1}, fun s hs => ⟨0, 1, one_pos, by simpa using hs⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [volume_real_axisParallelSquare]
  · rw [maxDisjointArea_singleton _ (by simp [volume_axisParallelSquare]),
      volume_real_axisParallelSquare _ zero_le_one, one_pow]

/--
**The covering problem of Rado.**
If the union of finitely many axis-parallel squares in the plane has unit area, how small can
the largest area covered by a pairwise disjoint subfamily of the squares be?

Formally, the question asks for the greatest lower bound of `maxDisjointArea S` over all finite
families `S` of axis-parallel squares (of arbitrary side lengths) whose union has area `1`.
In the notation of [BDJ10], this is Radó's constant $F(\text{square})$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado : IsGLB radoValues answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
**Radó's conjecture** [Ra28]: one can always find a disjoint subfamily covering at least a
quarter of the area of the union, and the constant $1/4$ cannot be improved. That is, Radó
conjectured that the answer to `covering_problem_of_rado` is $1/4$.

This was disproved by Ajtai [Aj73], see `covering_problem_of_rado.variants.ajtai`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.rado_conjecture : ¬ IsGLB radoValues (1 / 4) := by
  sorry

/--
Radó [Ra28] proved that one can always find a disjoint subfamily covering at least $1/9$ of the
area of the union.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.rado_lower_bound :
    1 / 9 ∈ lowerBounds radoValues := by
  sorry

/--
Ajtai [Aj73] constructed a finite family of axis-parallel squares (of two different sizes) such
that every pairwise disjoint subfamily covers at most $1/4 - 1/1728$ of the area of the union.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.ajtai :
    ∃ x ∈ radoValues, x ≤ 1 / 4 - 1 / 1728 := by
  sorry

/--
Bereg, Dumitrescu and Jiang [BDJ10] proved that one can always find a disjoint subfamily
covering at least $1/8.4797$ of the area of the union, i.e. $F(\text{square}) \ge 1/8.4797$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.lower_bound :
    1 / 8.4797 ∈ lowerBounds radoValues := by
  sorry

/--
Bereg, Dumitrescu and Jiang [BDJ10] proved that $F(\text{square}) \le 1/4 - 1/384$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.upper_bound (F : ℝ) (hF : IsGLB radoValues F) :
    F ≤ 1 / 4 - 1 / 384 := by
  sorry

end CoveringProblemOfRado

I resolved this by formalising the slot faithfully to the statement text as the open question `IsGLB radoValues answer(sorry)` (research open, exactly as the notes' fallback 'answer(sorry) for the infimum as in MoserWorm.lean'), and adding the refuted candidate as a separate `research solved` variant `covering_problem_of_rado.variants.rado_conjecture : ¬ IsGLB radoValues (1/4)`, plus the known bounds as further solved variants.
modeling_decisions: The list-page entry is a question ('how small can ... be?'), so the slot is stated with `answer(sorry)` for the greatest lower bound (`IsGLB radoValues answer(sorry)`), in the style of MoserWorm.lean, and tagged `research open` as the status says. Radó's refuted candidate answer 1/4 is NOT the slot statement; it is included separately as `covering_problem_of_rado.variants.rado_conjecture : ¬ IsGLB radoValues (1/4)` tagged `research solved`, together with Radó's 1/9 lower bound, Ajtai's construction (∃ x ∈ radoValues, x ≤ 1/4 − 1/1728), and the Bereg–Dumitrescu–Jiang bounds (1/8.4797 ∈ lowerBounds radoValues; any GLB F satisfies F ≤ 1/4 − 1/384).

Squares are modelled as OPEN axis-parallel squares `axisParallelSquare c r = {p | c 0 < p 0 < c 0 + r ∧ c 1 < p 1 < c 1 + r}` with `0 < r`. Hence `Disjoint` between two squares means their interiors do not overlap (squares touching only along boundaries count as disjoint), which is the reading required by the decomposition notes; areas are unaffected since boundaries are null.

A 'finite family' is a `Finset (Set ℝ²)` all of whose members satisfy `IsAxisParallelSquare`. Repeated squares are collapsed, which changes neither the union area nor the maximal disjoint-subfamily area (two equal open squares are never disjoint).

'Largest area covered by a disjoint subset' is `sSup` over subfamilies `I ⊆ S` with `(↑I).PairwiseDisjoint id` of `volume.real (⋃₀ ↑I)` (the area covered by the subfamily; equal to the sum of areas by disjointness). For finite `S` this set is finite and nonempty (the empty subfamily contributes 0), so `sSup` is a genuine maximum with no junk value.

Areas are real numbers via `volume.real` (Lebesgue measure on `ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`, the repo's standard plane). All sets involved (finite unions of bounded open squares) have finite measure, so `Measure.real` never hits its junk value; the unit-area hypothesis `volume.real (⋃₀ ↑S) = 1` automatically excludes the empty family.

The infimum is expressed with `IsGLB` rather than `sInf` to avoid junk values; the test lemma `one_mem_radoValues` proves the set is nonempty (and it is bounded below by 0), so the GLB exists and is unique, and `answer(sorry)` is genuinely constrained.
The normalisation 'union has unit area' is used literally (as in the statement) rather than the ratio |I|/|S| of Bereg–Dumitrescu–Jiang; the two are equivalent by scaling.

The upper bound of [BDJ10] is stated as a bound on the infimum (any `F` with `IsGLB radoValues F` satisfies `F ≤ 1/4 − 1/384`) rather than as an existence of a single family, since Wikipedia only asserts the inequality F(square) ≤ 1/4 − 1/384; Ajtai's result is stated as an explicit family because Wikipedia describes an explicit construction.

$$F(\text{square}) = \inf_S \max_I |I|,$$

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Covering problem of Rado

Tibor Radó (1928) asked: if the union of finitely many axis-parallel squares in the plane has
area one, what is the guaranteed maximum total area of a pairwise disjoint subfamily? In other
words, how small can the largest area covered by a disjoint subfamily be?

Radó proved that this quantity is at least $1/9$ and conjectured that it is exactly $1/4$.
Ajtai (1973) disproved the conjecture; the best known bounds (Bereg, Dumitrescu, Jiang, 2010) are
$1/8.4797 \le F(\mathrm{square}) \le 1/4 - 1/384$. The exact value is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/covering_problem_of_Rado)
- [Ra28] Radó, T., *Sur un problème relatif à un théorème de Vitali*,
  Fundamenta Mathematicae 11 (1928), 228–229.
- [Aj73] Ajtai, M., *The solution of a problem of T. Radó*,
  Bull. Acad. Polon. Sci. Sér. Sci. Math. Astronom. Phys. 21 (1973), 61–63.
- [BDJ10] Bereg, S., Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., *On covering problems of Rado*,
  Algorithmica 57 (2010), 538–561.
-/

open MeasureTheory
open scoped EuclideanGeometry ENNReal

namespace CoveringProblemOfRado

/-- An axis-parallel square in the plane, given by its lower-left corner and its side length. -/
structure AxisParallelSquare where
  /-- The lower-left corner of the square. -/
  corner : ℝ²
  /-- The side length of the square. -/
  side : ℝ
  side_pos : 0 < side

namespace AxisParallelSquare

/--
The set of points of an axis-parallel square, taken as an *open* square (its interior).
The boundary has measure zero, so this does not affect areas, and two squares are `Disjoint`
exactly when they do not overlap in a set of positive area (squares that only touch along
their boundaries count as disjoint).
-/
def toSet (q : AxisParallelSquare) : Set ℝ² :=
  {p | q.corner 0 < p 0 ∧ p 0 < q.corner 0 + q.side ∧ q.corner 1 < p 1 ∧ p 1 < q.corner 1 + q.side}

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem mem_toSet {q : AxisParallelSquare} {p : ℝ²} :
    p ∈ q.toSet ↔
      q.corner 0 < p 0 ∧ p 0 < q.corner 0 + q.side ∧ q.corner 1 < p 1 ∧ p 1 < q.corner 1 + q.side :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The (open) square is the preimage of a product of open intervals under `WithLp.ofLp`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem toSet_eq_preimage (q : AxisParallelSquare) :
    q.toSet = WithLp.ofLp ⁻¹'
      Set.pi Set.univ (fun i => Set.Ioo (q.corner i) (q.corner i + q.side)) := by
  ext p
  simp only [mem_toSet, Set.mem_preimage, Set.mem_pi, Set.mem_univ, Set.mem_Ioo, true_implies,
    Fin.forall_fin_two]
  tauto

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem isOpen_toSet (q : AxisParallelSquare) : IsOpen q.toSet := by
  rw [toSet_eq_preimage]
  exact (isOpen_set_pi Set.finite_univ fun _ _ => isOpen_Ioo).preimage (PiLp.continuous_ofLp 2 _)

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem toSet_nonempty (q : AxisParallelSquare) : q.toSet.Nonempty := by
  refine ⟨!₂[q.corner 0 + q.side / 2, q.corner 1 + q.side / 2], ?_⟩
  simp only [mem_toSet]
  norm_num
  exact q.side_pos

/-- The area of an axis-parallel square is the square of its side length. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem volume_toSet (q : AxisParallelSquare) : volume q.toSet = ENNReal.ofReal q.side ^ 2 := by
  rw [toSet_eq_preimage, (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin 2)).measure_preimage
    (MeasurableSet.univ_pi fun _ => measurableSet_Ioo).nullMeasurableSet, Real.volume_pi_Ioo]
  simp [pow_two]

end AxisParallelSquare

open AxisParallelSquare

/-- The total area covered by a finite family `S` of axis-parallel squares. -/
noncomputable def coveredArea (S : Finset AxisParallelSquare) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  volume (⋃ q ∈ S, q.toSet)

/--
The largest area covered by a subfamily of `S` consisting of pairwise disjoint squares.
(There are finitely many subfamilies, so the supremum is a maximum.)
-/
noncomputable def maxDisjointArea (S : Finset AxisParallelSquare) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (I : Finset AxisParallelSquare) (_ : I ⊆ S)
    (_ : (I : Set AxisParallelSquare).PairwiseDisjoint toSet), coveredArea I

/--
**Radó's constant** $F(\mathrm{square})$: the infimum, over all finite families $S$ of
axis-parallel squares whose union has area one, of the largest area covered by a subfamily of
$S$ consisting of pairwise disjoint squares.
-/
noncomputable def radoConstant : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (S : Finset AxisParallelSquare) (_ : coveredArea S = 1), maxDisjointArea S

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem coveredArea_singleton (q : AxisParallelSquare) :
    coveredArea {q} = ENNReal.ofReal q.side ^ 2 := by
  simp [coveredArea, volume_toSet]

/-- A disjoint subfamily cannot cover more area than the whole family. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem maxDisjointArea_le_coveredArea (S : Finset AxisParallelSquare) :
    maxDisjointArea S ≤ coveredArea S := by
  refine iSup₂_le fun I hI => iSup_le fun _ => measure_mono ?_
  exact Set.biUnion_subset_biUnion_left hI

/-- The unit square is a family of squares whose union has area one. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem coveredArea_unitSquare :
    coveredArea {(⟨0, 1, one_pos⟩ : AxisParallelSquare)} = 1 := by
  simp [coveredArea_singleton]

/-- Radó's constant is at most one. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem radoConstant_le_one : radoConstant ≤ 1 :=
  iInf₂_le_of_le _ coveredArea_unitSquare
    ((maxDisjointArea_le_coveredArea _).trans_eq coveredArea_unitSquare)

/--
**The covering problem of Rado.**
If the union of finitely many axis-parallel squares has unit area, how small can the largest
area covered by a pairwise disjoint subfamily of the squares be? That is, what is the value of
Radó's constant
$$F(\mathrm{square}) = \inf_S \max_I |{\textstyle\bigcup I}|,$$
where $S$ ranges over finite families of axis-parallel squares with $|\bigcup S| = 1$ and $I$
ranges over the subfamilies of $S$ consisting of pairwise disjoint squares?

Squares are modelled as open squares (`AxisParallelSquare.toSet`), so "disjoint" means that no
two squares of the subfamily overlap in a set of positive area; this does not change the
value of $F(\mathrm{square})$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado : radoConstant = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
**Radó's conjecture (disproved).**
Radó conjectured that every finite family of axis-parallel squares whose union has area one
contains a pairwise disjoint subfamily covering area at least $1/4$, i.e. that
$F(\mathrm{square}) \ge 1/4$ (together with the easy bound $F(\mathrm{square}) \le 1/4$ this
would give $F(\mathrm{square}) = 1/4$). Ajtai [Aj73] disproved this by constructing a family for
which every disjoint subfamily covers at most $1/4 - 1/1728$ of the area of the union.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.rado_conjecture : ¬ (1 / 4 ≤ radoConstant) := by
  sorry

/-- Radó [Ra28] proved that $F(\mathrm{square}) \ge 1/9$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.rado_lower_bound : 1 / 9 ≤ radoConstant := by
  sorry

/-- Ajtai [Aj73] proved that $F(\mathrm{square}) \le 1/4 - 1/1728$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.ajtai_upper_bound :
    radoConstant ≤ 1 / 4 - 1 / 1728 := by
  sorry

/--
Bereg, Dumitrescu and Jiang [BDJ10] proved that
$$\frac{1}{8.4797} \le F(\mathrm{square}) \le \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{384}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.bereg_dumitrescu_jiang_bounds :
    1 / 8.4797 ≤ radoConstant ∧ radoConstant ≤ 1 / 4 - 1 / 384 := by
  sorry

/--
**The case of equal squares.**
Radó's conjecture holds for families of congruent squares: if the union of finitely many
axis-parallel squares of the same side length has area one, then some pairwise disjoint
subfamily covers area at least $1/4$. This was proved independently by A. Sokolin, R. Rado
and V. A. Zalgaller.
-/

theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.equal_squares (S : Finset AxisParallelSquare) (s : ℝ)
    (hS : ∀ q ∈ S, q.side = s) (hS₁ : coveredArea S = 1) :
    1 / 4 ≤ maxDisjointArea S := by

covering_problem_of_rado.why: Stated as `radoConstant = answer(sorry)` (research open), where `radoConstant` is the infimum over finite families S of axis-parallel squares (positive side lengths) with area(⋃S) = 1 of the supremum (= maximum, finitely many subfamilies) over pairwise-disjoint subfamilies I ⊆ S of area(⋃I). Squares are modelled as open squares in ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) with Lebesgue `volume`, so `Disjoint` means non-overlapping interiors, as the decomposition notes prescribe. Bespoke problem-local definitions were needed (no notion of axis-parallel square / Radó constant exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib).

statement_blocks.covering_problem_of_rado:
/--
**The covering problem of Rado.**
If the union of finitely many axis-parallel squares has unit area, how small can the largest
area covered by a pairwise disjoint subfamily of the squares be? That is, what is the value of
Radó's constant
$$F(\mathrm{square}) = \inf_S \max_I |{\textstyle\bigcup I}|,$$
where $S$ ranges over finite families of axis-parallel squares with $|\bigcup S| = 1$ and $I$
ranges over the subfamilies of $S$ consisting of pairwise disjoint squares?

Squares are modelled as open squares (`AxisParallelSquare.toSet`), so "disjoint" means that no
two squares of the subfamily overlap in a set of positive area; this does not change the
value of $F(\mathrm{square})$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
